mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying, Exalted is He (لترون الجحيم): whoever read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ made it a quadriliteral verb, transferred from (رأى) in the sense of seeing with the eye; by its transfer to the quadriliteral it became transitive to two objects, one of which stands in place of the agent — namely the latent pronoun in (لترون), the object of a verb whose agent is not named [i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)] — and (الجحيم) is the second object. Whoever read the tāʾ with fatḥa made it a triliteral verb not transferred to the quadriliteral, so he made it transitive to a single object, because in both readings it is from seeing with the eye.
Its origin is «لترأيون». The vowel of the hamza was thrown onto the rāʾ, as was done in (يرى) and (ترى) by way of lightening (tashīl) — a lightening that is constant in this form wherever it occurs as an imperfect. So «لتريون» remained. When the yāʾ was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa, it was changed into an alif, and it was elided because of its quiescence together with the quiescence of the wāw after it, so «لترون» remained. Then the doubled nūn entered, and the nūn of inflection was elided for the indeclinability (bināʾ); and the wāw was given ḍamma because of its quiescence together with the quiescence of the first [element] of the doubled nūn.
It is not permissible to give the wāw of (لترون) a hamza on account of its ḍamma, because its vowel is accidental, due to the meeting of two quiescent letters — namely the wāw and the first of the doubled [letter]. Do you not see that you did not restore the lām of the verb, which had been elided before the wāw because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the wāw of the pronoun? Yet the wāw of the pronoun has been vowelled because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the first of the doubled nūn of emphasis. So since its vowel is not taken into account, the lām of the verb was not restored, and giving it a hamza is not permissible. The second one is like it. Nor is it permissible to elide the wāw for the meeting of two quiescent letters, because the lām of the verb before it has already been elided, and because before it is a fatḥa, and a fatḥa does not indicate a wāw were it elided.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying (عين اليقين): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because its meaning is «لتعاينُنّها عيانا يقينا» (you will surely see it with your own eyes, a seeing of certainty).
